evals.prompt: I want Claude Code to render a 15 second vertical 1080x1920 motion graphics video at 60 fps from a single canvas page, no framework. How should the page and the render script work, and what encode and motion blur settings should I use?
assertions: The page exposes a window.seek(t) (or draw(t)) function that paints the frame for time t, with no timers, CSS transitions or requestAnimationFrame during the render
Randomness is seeded (e.g. mulberry32), never Math.random
Encodes with libx264 / H.264, yuv420p pixel format, CRF 16
Motion blur by rendering 4 subframes per frame and blending them (ffmpeg tmix)
Waits for fonts to load (document.fonts.ready) before capturing canvas text

evals.prompt: In my code-rendered UI morph video the cursor and the container width change target several times and the motion jumps whenever I restart the spring. The tab indicator also looks stiff. How do I fix this while keeping the render deterministic?
assertions: Do not restart the spring: sum one closed-form spring per target change, each starting at its own time (a track() over [time, value] keys)
Keeps the value a pure function of time, so any frame can be rendered without simulating earlier frames
Tab indicator stretches by putting its leading and trailing edges on different springs, the leading edge stiffer
For a loop, the last frame must equal the first, including cursor position and velocity

evals.prompt: Make me a 30 second cartoon starring Clawd, the Claude mascot, finding a lost sandwich. Before you write code, what rules will you follow for how it looks and moves?
assertions: No text: no captions, titles, signs or speech-bubble words; reactions are painted marks such as !, ?, sweat or hearts
Everything is flat 2D painted with p5.brush (paint()/inkLine()); never project 3D or rotate in perspective, turns use drawn key views
Every seam gets a transition (brush wipe, iris, match cut, cut on action and so on); never start on a hard frame or just stop
Clawd is big: about 20-28 u in a medium shot, 40-70 in close-ups
Writes a storyboard before any scene code

evals.prompt: My Opus-made launch video looks a bit mid. What exact steps should Claude run to review and improve the render before I post it?
assertions: Renders a contact sheet with ffmpeg (fps=2, tiled 6x5) plus a strip around fast actions and a phone-size test at 360 px wide
Scores each review 1-10 on criteria such as hook in the first 2 s, readability at phone size, motion quality, variety, brand accuracy and sound sync
Fixes the 3 worst problems and repeats until every score is 8 or higher

Hunts named failures: overlapping text during swaps, sliding instead of easing, corner labels and frame borders, centered-on-gradient shots, blurry scaled text, a dead beat, a stutter at the loop seam
Re-renders only the affected seconds after fixes

evals.prompt: Should I use HyperFrames or Remotion for agent-made product videos, and if HyperFrames, how do I set it up for Claude Code?
assertions: Installs the HyperFrames agent skills with npx skills add heygen-com/hyperframes (choosing Core Skills), or npx hyperframes skills update for non-interactive/CI
Starts a fresh agent chat after install and asks it to use /hyperframes
Remotion fits teams already writing React (components, design system, typed inputs); HyperFrames needs no React or build step and is Apache 2.0
Notes Opus defaults to a zero-dependency index.html + Playwright + ffmpeg route and skips frameworks unless explicitly asked

evals.prompt: My code-rendered product reel has no music track supplied. How should the audio be made and synced to the picture?
assertions: Synthesizes the score and SFX in code on the same timeline as the picture
When a track is supplied, measures it with librosa into a beats.json with bpm, beats, downbeats (every 4th beat) and onset hits
State changes land on beats, big moments on downbeats, SFX on hits
Targets a loudness of -14 LUFS for the final mix
